Hi Olivia — thanks for the specific questions. Below are concise answers; I'll follow up with the completed RFI workbook and the additional evidence pack by end of day 6/06.

1) Retention (raw prompts): By default, raw prompts provided to the hosted API are stored in encrypted request logs for 90 days for the purposes of debugging, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. Customers on Redwood Private or on a dedicated plan can opt-in to zero-retention or shorter retention windows and/or customer-managed keys. We can add a contract clause for prompt retention TTL.

2) Caching: Model KV caches are ephemeral, tenant-scoped, and remain in GPU memory or ephemeral attached storage. They are not persisted to multi-tenant long-term storage and are not shared across customers. We never surface cached prompt fragments to other tenants.

3) Key access & debugging: With Redwood-managed keys, a small number of authorized engineering personnel can access decrypted data for emergency debugging under strict ticketing and MFA controls; access is logged and subject to IAM approvals and periodic review. For customers requiring stronger guarantees, we recommend customer-managed KMS/HSM where keys are inaccessible to Redwood (bring-your-own-key). We'll mark this as a negotiable clause in the DPA.

4) Incident notification SLA: We publish a standard incident classification table. For security incidents involving customer data (P1), notification is within 72 hours of confirmation; P2 within 5 business days with status updates. Root-cause analysis and remediation timelines vary by severity but will be provided as deliverables.

5) Processor/controller: For our hosted API, Redwood operates as a processor under customer direction. For private deployments where the customer manages the control plane or is on-prem, the customer typically assumes controller responsibilities. We'll include this explicit language in the DPA annex.

Attachments we are providing in the evidence pack: SOC2_TypeII_report_2027.pdf (PDF, redacted), Key_Management_Integration_Guide.pdf (PDF), DPA_Annex_Template_Redwood.pdf (PDF). A full subprocessor list and redlined DPA are available on request; we can provide a redacted subprocessor CSV for your procurement team.
